Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.application.chat

Class DelegationServiceImpl

java.lang.Object
com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.application.chat.DelegationServiceImpl
All Implemented Interfaces:
DelegationService
@Service public class DelegationServiceImpl extends Object implements DelegationService
Default DelegationService implementation (US-12-002).

Steps every delegate(...) invocation runs through, in order:

  1. Re-fetch the parent agent (REQ-AGT-014 — the team list applies the live-config rule). Missing parent → InvalidDelegationTargetException.
  2. Assert command.targetMemberId() is in parent.team(). This is the runtime side of REQ-AGT-013 — defense in depth on top of EPIC-06's write-time validators.
  3. Resolve the target agent. Missing target, OR cross-owner target (REQ-AGT-012) → InvalidDelegationTargetException.
  4. Assert the target's own team is empty — single-level rule (REQ-AGT-013) — re-checked at runtime.
  5. Build a minimal ChatRequest for the target: NO parent conversation history (REQ-AGT-015), target's own system prompt / sampling / tools / MCP servers, filesystem MCP per-user root materialized under the parent's owner (REQ-MCP-005 scopes per the calling user, who is identical to the target's owner thanks to REQ-AGT-012). The target's tools never include any delegate descriptor — the target is a leaf by the single-level rule.
  6. Invoke LlmChatClient.call(ChatRequest) synchronously (REQ-AGT-015 — the user sees only the parent's stream, not the sub-agent's incremental output).
  7. Return DelegationService.DelegationResult carrying the target id + the sub-agent's final text. NO persistence — REQ-AGT-015's "B's exchanges SHALL NOT be persisted" is enforced structurally: this class has no ConversationRepository dependency and an ArchUnit rule (in LayeringArchTest) prevents a future refactor from introducing one.

Catalog / scope dependencies are kept narrow: only what is needed to resolve tools and MCP server names against the same catalogs the parent's ChatRequestBuilder uses. Tool / MCP drift (an agent referencing a name no longer in the catalog) surfaces as AgentConfigurationDriftException, matching the parent path's behavior — mapped to 500 by the generic handler.
